cards.text: This passage opens with a word I wish it didn't: Again. Again the Israelites did evil in the sight of the LORD, so He delivered them into the hand of Midian. The Midianites are a people descended from Midian, a son of Abraham and Keturah (Genesis 25:1-2).

cards.question: Israel stays in the hand of Midian for ___ years.

cards.text: The hand of Midian prevails against Israel. It gets so bad that the Israelites start preparing shelters for themselves.

cards.question: Because of the Midianites, where do the Israelites prepare their shelters?

answers.text: Up in the mountains and caves

cards.text: Whenever Israel plants crops, the Midianites, Amalekites and other people of the east come up and invade. The Amalekites are descendants of Amalek, a grandson of Esau (Genesis 36:12).

cards.question: The invaders camp against Israel as far as Gaza and ___ the produce of the land.

cards.text: They leave Israel nothing to live on, not even sheep, oxen or donkeys. That's like pulling a fresh batch out of the oven, turning around for ONE second, and finding the cooling rack EMPTY, not a crumb left!

cards.question: The Midianites pour in with their livestock and their tents. What does the Bible say they come in like?
True or false: the Midianites and their camels could be counted.

cards.text: Israel is greatly impoverished by Midian. So the Israelites cry out to the LORD.

cards.question: When Israel cries out because of Midian, the LORD sends them a ___ with a message.

cards.text: The message starts with what the LORD has done. He brought them up out of Egypt, out of the house of slavery, and He drove out their oppressors and gave them their land.

cards.question: Then the LORD reminds Israel of something He told them. What was it?

answers.text: Not to fear the gods of the Amorites
Not to make peace with the Midianites
Not to plant their crops near Gaza

cards.question: True or false: in the prophet's message, the LORD says Israel obeyed Him.

cards.text: Then the angel of the LORD comes and sits under the oak in Ophrah that belongs to Joash the Abiezrite. And right there, Joash's son Gideon is threshing wheat, hiding it from the Midianites.

cards.question: Where is Gideon threshing his wheat to hide it from the Midianites?
The angel of the LORD appears to Gideon and tells him the LORD is with him. What does the angel call Gideon?

cards.text: If an angel called ME a mighty man of valor while I was lying in that junk drawer, I'd have turned around to see who he was talking to! Gideon says, “Please, my Lord,” and then asks why, if the LORD is with them, all this has happened to them.

cards.question: Gideon asks where all the LORD's wonders went. Which wonder does he say his fathers told him about?

answers.text: Bringing them up out of Egypt

cards.question: True or false: Gideon tells the angel that the LORD has forsaken Israel and handed them over to Midian.

cards.text: Then the LORD turns to Gideon, and what He says next is no small talk.

cards.question: The LORD turns to Gideon and gives him a job. What is it?

cards.text: The LORD tells him to go in the strength he has, and asks, “Am I not sending you?” That's a question with ONE right answer, like when the boss leans in and says, “Got a minute?”

cards.question: Gideon asks how he can save Israel. He says his clan is the ___ in Manasseh.
True or false: Gideon says he is the oldest in his father's house.

cards.text: “Surely I will be with you,” the LORD replies. Then He tells Gideon he will strike down all the Midianites as one man.
But Gideon wants to be sure who he's talking to.

cards.question: Gideon asks for a ___ that it's really the LORD speaking with him.

cards.text: He asks Him not to leave until he comes back with an offering. And the LORD says, “I will stay until you return.”

cards.question: Gideon goes in and gets his offering ready. What does he bring out under the oak?

answers.text: A young goat and unleavened bread
A lamb and a jar of honey
A dove and a jar of oil

cards.text: The angel of God tells him to lay the meat and the unleavened bread on this rock and pour out the broth. And Gideon does it.

cards.question: The angel of the LORD touches the meat and the bread with the tip of his staff. What happens?

answers.text: Fire flares up from the rock
Water pours out of the rock
The rock splits right in two

cards.question: True or false: after the fire, the angel of the LORD stays right there in Gideon's sight.

cards.text: That's when Gideon realizes it was the angel of the LORD. It's like griping to a nice stranger in the elevator about how the company's run, and then he walks into your meeting and sits at the head of the table.

cards.question: Gideon cries out, “Oh no, Lord GOD!” What does he say happened?

answers.text: He saw the angel face to face
He made the angel wait too long
He gave the angel too little

cards.question: The LORD says to him, “Peace be with you. Do not be afraid,” True or false: the LORD tells Gideon he will not die.

cards.text: So Gideon builds an altar to the LORD right there. The text says it still stands in Ophrah of the Abiezrites to this day.

cards.question: What does Gideon call the altar he builds in Ophrah?

cards.text: On that very night, the LORD tells Gideon to take his father's young bull and a second bull seven years old. And this job is a whole lot closer to home.

cards.question: What does the LORD tell Gideon to tear down?
Beside his father's altar to Baal, Gideon must also cut down the ___.

cards.text: Then he's to build a proper altar to the LORD on top of this stronghold. And with the wood of that Asherah pole, he's to offer the second bull as a burnt offering.
So Gideon takes ten of his servants and does what the LORD told him.

cards.question: True or false: Gideon and his servants do the job in broad daylight.
Why does Gideon tear down Baal's altar at night?

answers.text: He fears his father's household and the city
The LORD told him to keep it all a secret
His servants could only work after dark

cards.text: Morning comes, and the men of the city get up. Friend, if I were Gideon, I'd be back in that winepress by sunrise, threshing NOTHING, just hiding!

cards.question: True or false: when the men of the city get up in the morning, Baal's altar is still standing.

cards.text: “Who did this?” they say to one another. They investigate thoroughly, and they're told, “Gideon son of Joash did it.”

cards.question: The men of the city tell Joash to bring out his son. They say Gideon must ___.

cards.text: Now Joash has a whole crowd standing against him. It's like opening the work group chat to fifty messages, and EVERY one of them is about you.

cards.question: True or false: Joash hands Gideon over to the men of the city.

cards.text: Joash asks them, “Are you contending for Baal? Are you trying to save him?” Then he warns that whoever pleads Baal's case will be put to death by morning.

cards.question: Joash tells the crowd what Baal should do if Baal is a god. What is it?

cards.text: So on that day, Gideon gets a new name: Jerubbaal.

cards.question: Gideon is called Jerubbaal because he tore down Baal's altar. What does Jerubbaal mean?

cards.text: And that's where we'll leave it for now, friend. The guy from the winepress has a brand new name, and trust me, his story is just getting warmed up.

findings.problem: The number of years (seven) can only be guessed. Card 1 gives no context that would let a baker reason toward seven over forty or twenty, so it is pure luck. Stop 1 already has several other discovery questions (cards 4, 8, 16 and 17), so most of its choice cards are no longer informed guesses. Tell the seven years on a story card and ask something the baker can reason out instead.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

findings.problem: Card 3 says only that the Israelites prepare shelters. Nothing on it points toward mountains and caves rather than Jericho or the Jordan, so the pick is luck. Card 3 needs a hint, such as that they're hiding from the invaders, or this should be a different question.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: The setup line "this job is a whole lot closer to home" rules out the wrong answer "The camp of the Midianites" on card 2. That leaves the baker only the two answers tied to Gideon's family.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.
